title: Per-route dynamic burst credits and negative-balance invoice handling PRD
creator: Lena Ortiz
description: Define requirements and acceptance criteria for a per-route dynamic burst credit system and the operational billing behavior when accounts go into a negative balance. This includes API/Console surface changes, server-side allocation logic, invoicing adjustments, and operator override flows.
background: Customers have asked for finer control over burst capacity per API route (e.g., embeddings vs. generation) while preserving a global credit pool. Current behavior applies burst credits at the tenant level only, which leads to noisy spikes on a single hot route and poor cost attribution. Separately, when accounts exceed prepaid credits or quotas we create negative balances but lack a clear operator playbook for invoice adjustments and automated remediation windows. This PRD aligns product, billing, and ops on a consistent model.
scope: In scope: per-route burst allocation algorithm, API fields for route-level burst configs, Console UI for route entitlements, billing logic for negative balances (grace windows, automated invoice adjustments), admin override and reconciliation flows, monitoring and alerts. Out of scope: new pricing tiers or changes to base per-token pricing.
requirements: Enable customers to assign a percentage of their global burst credit pool to individual routes (min 0%, max 100%).
Default behavior: if no per-route allocation exists, routes may consume from shared pool subject to global burst policy.
Burst consumption must be tracked per-route and exposed in usage APIs and Console with token-level granularity and approximate cost attribution.

When a tenant exhausts both route allocation and shared pool, requests will follow the configured fallback policy: soft-throttle with 429 after a configurable soft-window (default 15s) or route-level fallback to a cheaper model if configured.

When prepay credits or invoice balance becomes negative, apply a configurable grace window (default 72 hours) before blocking high-cost routes; during the window allow lower-cost routes depending on plan entitlements.

Automated invoicing: if negative balance persists beyond N days (configurable, default 7), system generates an adjustment invoice and a collection task; adjustments must include detailed per-route usage contributing to the balance.
Operators must be able to issue manual invoice credits and mark reconciliation reasons; these actions must create immutable audit entries and trigger billing re-calculation.
All behavior must be deterministic under concurrent requests (no race conditions causing double-consumption of burst credits).
Expose new telemetry events: burst_alloc_change, burst_consumed_route, burst_refunded, negative_balance_entered, negative_balance_resolved, manual_invoice_credit_applied.
Console UX: add per-route entitlement page with editable allocation slider, projected monthly cost estimate, and historical burst consumption chart (90d).
API backwards compatibility: new fields must be optional and default to current behavior for existing customers.
Provide migration notes and a bulk API to set per-route allocations for enterprise customers.
Security & data: billing audit logs must include user and operator identifiers and be retained according to existing retention policy (90 days visible in Console, 365 days in backend logs).
acceptance_criteria: Per-route allocation can be set via API and Console; allocations persist and are visible in GET usage responses.
Burst consumption attributed to routes matches telemetry within 2% in synthetic and production smoke tests over a 24h window.
Under heavy concurrent requests to the same route, burst credit counters remain consistent (unit tests and load tests prove idempotency and no double-counting).
Default fallback policy triggers 429 after the soft-window when no burst credits remain; configurable route fallback to cheaper model occurs when configured and tested.
Negative-balance flow: entering negative balance creates telemetry event and applies soft-grace policy; after 72 hours high-cost routes are blocked in canary tests unless credits are added.
Automated adjustment invoice is generated with per-route breakdown when negative balance persists beyond the configured threshold; invoice lines reconcile to recorded usage within 0.5% divergence.
Operator manual credit flow updates invoices and creates audit entries; reconciliation view in Console shows before/after balances and reason field.
New telemetry events are emitted and searchable in the observability pipeline within the standard retention window.
Console UI tests validate slider behavior, projections, and historical charts render for accounts with at least 90 days of data.
API backwards compatibility regression tests ensure existing clients without new fields behave unchanged.
Security review sign-off not required for initial rollout but audit log retention and operator permissions validated by Security.
Documentation: public docs, billing FAQ, and migration guide published before GA release.
Metrics: GA monitored metrics include route-level burst utilization, number of negative-balance events, average time-to-resolution, and number of manual invoice credits issued.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 - Canary (2 weeks): implement feature gated behind tenant flag; enable for internal tenants and 3 pilot customers. Collect telemetry and validate acceptance criteria.
Phase 2 - Limited GA (4 weeks): open to self-serve customers with opt-in; provide migration bulk API and support playbook for account managers.
Phase 3 - GA (after sign-off): enable by default for new tenants and provide migration tooling for existing tenants with clear rollback path.
Operator training and runbook: publish playbook for negative-balance remediation and manual invoice credit process concurrent with Phase 2.
Communication: customer blog, release notes, and dedicated support bulletin for enterprise customers two weeks before GA.
test_cases: Unit tests for allocation arithmetic and edge values (0%, 100%).
Concurrency load test: 10k RPS to single route from multiple clients to verify no credit double-spend and stable counters.
E2E billing test: create negative balance scenario, advance time in staging, assert automated invoice generation and contents.
UI tests: slider change persists, projection updates correctly, chart shows expected historical series when seeded with synthetic data.
Fallback behavior test: configure route fallback to cheaper model and validate traffic switches under exhaustion.
Operator flow test: apply manual credit and verify invoice recalculation and audit log entry.
monitoring_and_metrics: alerts: high-negative-balance-rate (>5% active tenants/day) and burst-allocation-anomaly (>20% sudden spike)
